## Changes

- Stops suggesting a route home when KSA records a completed return. With Life Support enabled, DeltaVMap clears the automatic mission route and keeps a manually selected route on the current map.

## Compatibility

Validated against KSA build version **2026.11.25.5949**.

## Installation

Extract into `Documents\My Games\Kitten Space Agency\mods\DeltaVMap\`.
Requires [StarMap](https://github.com/StarMapLoader/StarMap).

listing.name: DeltaVMap
listing.abstract: An interactive, auto-generated delta-v subway map and transfer-window planner for Kitten Space Agency.
listing.description:
An interactive, auto-generated delta-v subway map and transfer-window planner for [Kitten Space Agency](https://ahwoo.com/app/100000/kitten-space-agency). It reads every star system of the loaded universe live, so it works with any system, stock or modded, single-star or multi-star, with no per-system setup.

![The Delta-V Map rooted at Earth](ksa-image:delta-v-map)

This mod is written against the [StarMap loader](https://github.com/StarMapLoader/StarMap).

Validated against KSA build version 2026.11.16.5901.

## What it does

The map tells you "where can I go from where I am and for how much delta-v".
The transfer-window layer answers the "and when do I leave" question.

Both are generated from the loaded `CelestialSystem`, recurse through every star system, star, planet, moon, asteroid and comet, and read each body's mass, radius, SOI, orbit and atmosphere. Nothing is hardcoded.

All numbers are closed-form patched-conic estimates (Hohmann transfers with Oberth-combined departure and capture, no iterative solver), so the whole map is fast and every transfer is cached once per loaded system.

The delta-v figures are the idealized optimal values, so they assume a well-timed, well-flown transfer. A "piloting-margin percentage" slider is available.

Retrograde transfer-window countdowns use the stock timing rule and have not been validated independently. Plane-change costs between stars orbiting a barycenter are approximate because they use orbital speeds derived from the hub's mass.

## Features

### Delta-v subway map

- **Ego-centric metro layout.** The body you are currently in is the root; the map re-roots automatically on the next open after an SOI change or a crossing into another star system, and Shift-Click re-roots to any body on demand.
- **Every star system.** The other star systems sit apart from your map as small graphs of their own, joined to your star by a dashed interstellar line (not to scale). Click one to open it and plan a trip there; the **System** menu roots the map in any of them.
- **Accurate budgets.** Closed-form Hohmann transfers with Oberth-combined ejection and capture, a per-body state ladder (surface, low orbit, stationary, SOI edge, intercept) and a "you are here" marker at your actual orbit.
- **Route planning.** Click any body to highlight the exact route from your current state, with a per-segment breakdown. The route total stays pinned at the bottom of the side panel, below everything that scrolls. Toggles for from-surface, landing, aerobraking, plane change and a return trip, plus a piloting-margin percentage to budget for non-optimal flying.
- **Vehicle comparison.** A bar under the pinned total compares the selected route against your ship's available delta-v. Under the bar, a crewed vessel shows whether its supplies last the mission, and an uncrewed one shows how long its probe core power lasts.
- **Bound and open orbits.** An orbit counts as open or bound the way the game does, so an orbit very close to parabolic is handled the same in every part of the map.
- **Readable at scale.** Node-symbol vocabulary with a legend, collapsible side-panel sections, search / focus / isolate, and automatic minor-body aggregation so a dense system (thousands of asteroids) stays usable. A planet with hundreds of small moons keeps its inner moons as lanes and groups the outer ones. Click any "+N" group to list its members with their size and orbit, and click one to put it on the map and plan the route to it. Wide moon fans and long planet rows continue in rows below, joined by a dashed line that carries no delta-v. The **Wrap wide systems** toggle in **Options > Layout** turns this on or off, and it is on by default.
- **Three layout modes**, switched from the on-canvas toggle or the Options menu. Gravity-well wraps a wide system into shelves, one below the other, so it is the best mode for a tall window:

| Cumulative-down (default) | Gravity-well | Spring |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Cumulative-down layout](ksa-image:delta-v-map) | ![Gravity-well layout](ksa-image:layout-gravity-well) | ![Spring layout](ksa-image:layout-spring) |

### Interstellar routes

A trip to another star system is a route like any other: click the system, or a star, planet or moon in it. Pick the cruise speed (0.001 c, 0.01 c, 0.1 c, a slider, or MAX for the fastest your vessel can pay for) and the route panel shows:

- the departure and capture burns, including the Oberth effect and the plane change,
- the coast time and the cheapest trip at any speed,
- the total against your vessel's delta-v,
- a fuel estimate: the game's own interstellar burn model for an antimatter drive, the rocket equation otherwise.

Like the stock planner it is Newtonian. A button opens the stock Transfer Planner on its Interstellar plan for the trip. The mission block below (return trip, stay, mission time, Set as mission) works for these routes too, with the mission time counted at the cruise speed.

### Missions and life support

The map reads the mission of your vessel, set in the vehicle editor or in flight, and plans with it. In the editor it reads the mission of the vehicle you are editing.

- **Mission route.** When the map opens and nothing is selected, the mission destination is selected with the mission's arrival (flyby, orbit or land) and trip (one way or return). After the vessel has arrived on a return mission, the route is the way home. Your own pick is never overridden: the mission route is applied again only when the mission itself changes, or when you press **MISSION ROUTE**. The map selects the mission route by itself only while the universe uses life support, because without it the game does not plan with the mission either; **MISSION ROUTE** works in both cases.
- **Mission time.** The route panel shows the stock mission timing: out, stay, back and total. The stay is rounded up to the next return window, and the time to wait for that window is shown as its own row. For the mission route the stay comes from the mission; for any other route, set the **STAY AT DESTINATION** field in days.
- **Supplies.** For a crewed vessel, when the universe uses life support, a line under the vehicle bar compares the air, water, food and CO2 scrubbers aboard against the whole mission time. It says either that supplies are enough, or which supply is short, by how long, and in which habitat zone. It uses the game's life support forecast.
- **Probe power.** For an uncrewed vessel, a line shows how long the probe core power lasts, compared with the mission time. It is a snapshot of the current power balance, so sunlight, attitude and the loads you switch on change it.
- **Set as mission.** The **SET AS MISSION** button writes the selected route into the vessel's mission: destination, arrival, trip, stay and, for an interstellar route, the cruise speed. It works in flight and in the editor, and only for a body the stock mission picker can target. A mission to the home body is low orbit only. In flight it replaces the whole plan, while the stock **UPDATE MISSION** button changes only the destination.
- **Stock Transfer Planner.** In flight, an in-system route has a button that opens the stock Transfer Planner on its Hohmann plan with your vessel as the source and the route target as the destination, when the planner lists that target.

### Transfer windows

The timing companion to the map. For the root body and every sibling sharing its parent, it shows the optimal phase angle, the live current phase, a countdown to the next window, the synodic period, the ejection angle and the transfer time, in a compact list plus a live polar phase-clock. A **Stay** column and the row tooltip show how long to wait at the destination for the return window, and the shortest round trip.

![The transfer-window list and phase clock](ksa-image:transfer-windows)

A separate, opt-in layer draws the same data in the game's 3D map mode: the optimal-departure marker on the destination's real orbit (where it will be when the window opens), the planet-star-planet phase angle, and an ejection-angle gizmo at the departure body.

![The transfer-window overlay in the game map mode](ksa-image:map-mode-overlay)

## Installation

1. Install [StarMap](https://github.com/StarMapLoader/StarMap) 0.5.3 or later.
2. Download the latest release from the [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Maximilian-Nesslauer/KSA-DeltaVMap/releases) tab or from [SpaceDock](https://spacedock.info/mod/4294/DeltaVMap).
3. Extract into `Documents\My Games\Kitten Space Agency\mods\DeltaVMap\`.
4. The game auto-discovers new mods and prompts you to enable them. Alternatively, add to `Documents\My Games\Kitten Space Agency\manifest.toml`:

```toml
[[mods]]
id = "DeltaVMap"
enabled = true
```

Open the map from **Mods > Delta-V Map**, in flight and in the editor.

## Dependencies

| Package | Purpose | Tested version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [StarMap](https://github.com/StarMapLoader/StarMap) | Mod loader, version 0.5.3 or later, required at runtime (see [Installation](#installation)) | 0.5.4 |

## Build dependencies

Required only to build the mod from source. Targets **.NET 10**.

| Package | Source | Tested Version |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [StarMap.API](https://github.com/StarMapLoader/StarMap) | NuGet | 0.5.2 |
| [Lib.Harmony](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Lib.Harmony) | NuGet | 2.4.2 |

## Mod compatibility

- Known conflicts: none
